title: PrivacyChoicesLink
wrapsNative: Button with Label and the Monarch link style, opening sheet(isPresented:content:) with a NavigationStack, a Form with one Toggle (switch), a Link and ToolbarItem Cancel and Save
summary: A recipe, not a component: a "Your privacy choices" row in settings that opens a sheet with one switch to allow or stop the sale or sharing of personal information.
whenToUse: In settings, for people in regions where they may opt out of the sale or sharing of their personal information (opt-out regimes such as the California rules).
whenNotToUse: Where consent is asked before any optional use (opt-in regimes), ask with the full consent preferences instead. For tracking across other companies' apps and websites, iOS requires the AppTrackingTransparency prompt; this switch does not replace it.
api: Button { … } label: { Label("Your privacy choices", systemImage: "hand.raised") }.buttonStyle(.monarchLink(.standalone))
.sheet(isPresented: $isOpen) { NavigationStack { Form { Toggle("Allow sale or sharing", isOn: $draft) } } }

states.name: hidden
states.description: Outside opt-out regions the row is not shown.

states.name: open
states.description: A sheet with what sale or sharing means, the switch with its help line, the policy link, and Cancel and Save in the toolbar. The switch starts from the stored choice.

states.name: locked by signal
states.description: When the account carries a Global Privacy Control opt-out, the switch is off and disabled and the help line says why.

states.name: saved
states.description: Save stores the switch; Cancel leaves the stored choice unchanged.

appearance: The row is a standalone Monarch link with an icon. The sheet is a system Form with the standard switch, the body text style for the explanation and an external Monarch link to the policy, all in the theme colours.
platformNotes: The web's PrivacyChoicesLink is a footer link component with a dialog and its own strings. On iOS it is a recipe: a settings row opening a sheet with a Form, the native place for a setting. A native app receives no browser Global Privacy Control header, so the lock applies only when the app knows of a signal for the account (for example from its website); otherwise leave it out. The web's showIn regimes are the app's own region check. The web shows a policy link from policyHref or policyLink; here it is a Link. The official California privacy choices icon is the app's to add as an image; the recipe uses an SF Symbol. Android composes the same recipe.
accessibility: The row is a button whose label is the text; the icon is part of the Label.
The switch is a standard Toggle, read as "Allow sale or sharing" with its on or off value.
When the switch is locked, the reason is the visible section footer, which VoiceOver reads with the form.
Cancel and Save are standard toolbar buttons in the cancellation and confirmation placements.
The policy link is a standard Link marked as external.
edgeCases: Show the row only where the opt-out applies, decided by the app's region logic.
Opening the sheet starts from the stored choice, so a cancelled change does not linger.
A signal lock keeps sale and sharing off whatever was stored before.
